summary: Self-improving agent that runs ML experiments in a loop, 21k+ stars. Coined 'agentic engineering' — human writes the loop contract, AI runs the inner loop autonomously.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the outer-loop sovereignty and gated human confirmation pattern mirrors AgentForge's AwaitingPlanApproval gate, but AutoResearch is for ML experiments, not software delivery pipelines.

summary: Framework distinguishing vibe coding (floor raising) from agentic engineering (ceiling raising). 9 rules for shifting execution/bookkeeping to AI models via loops, planning, generation, review, and disk state.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — philosophical framing already embodied in AgentForge's design. No specific implementable gap identified.

summary: LangGraph 2.0 (Feb 2026) added node caching, deferred nodes as fan-in barriers, per-node timeouts, graceful shutdown, and MCP servers as first-class graph nodes with streaming.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses CLI subprocess model (not graph nodes); per-node timeouts are interesting but HID-163 (telemetry) and HID-167 (retry) must land first to give timeout data meaning.

source: Episodic-Semantic Memory Architecture for Long-Horizon Scientific Agents (arxiv 2605.17625)
summary: Dual-Process Memory Architecture decomposes episodic (what the agent did) and semantic (domain facts) memory with domain-specific consolidation, showing +29.6 on temporal queries and +23.1 on multi-hop reasoning.
relevanceToAgentForge: High in principle — but HID-188 already tracks cross-run episodic memory injection into planner/executor. The separation of episodic from semantic is a useful architectural nuance for whoever implements HID-188.

summary: 7-layer memory system (working, short-term, episodic, long-term, procedural, core, predictive) with FSRS spaced repetition, Hebbian learning, sleep consolidation, and emotional tagging for LLM agents.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — extremely complex (15 mechanisms) and speculative for a 1-2 run implementation. HID-188 already tracks the episodic memory gap at an appropriate scope.

source: AREX: Recursively Self-Improving Agent for Deep Research (arxiv 2607.21461)
summary: RSI agent alternating inner research loop with outer self-improvement loop; trains 4B dense and 122B MoE models via agentic mid-training and long-horizon RL to improve their own research outputs.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — requires RL training infrastructure (red flag per Phase 3 rules). The inner/outer loop concept is interesting but AgentForge's AddressingReview→AIReview loop already implements a bounded equivalent without RL.

summary: Open-source framework for building, evaluating, and evolving LLM agents through iterative feedback loops — agents are constructed, assessed, and optimized similarly to CI pipelines.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — self-evolving via RL/optimization is a red flag (Phase 3 disqualification). The CI-pipeline analogy is already AgentForge's core design.

source: Self-Improvements in Modern Agentic Systems: A Survey (arxiv 2607.13104)
summary: Survey covering reflection, self-critique, memory consolidation, and RL-based self-improvement patterns across modern agentic systems.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium as reference — no single implementable piece surfaced beyond what HID-186/HID-188/HID-93 already track. Useful as background reading for implementers.

summary: Microsoft merged AutoGen and Semantic Kernel into unified Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 (April 2026). Legacy AutoGen moved to maintenance-only; community fork AG2 continues independently.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses CLI subprocess model (Claude Code, Codex), not AutoGen-style multi-agent messaging. No integration point.

source: PILOT in the Loop: Live Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Agents (arxiv 2608.26530)
summary: PILOT enables live self-improvement during execution for long-horizon agents by maintaining a reflective inner monologue that updates a compact policy sketch used to guide subsequent steps.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the in-flight policy sketch is conceptually close to plan revision (HID-186). However HID-186 already tracks stage-level partial retry. No new gap identified.
